description:
# THE GRAND SONGBOOK OF 1040 BF
### Waluigi's Definitive Audit of Campaign Ballads, Shanties & Unsanctioned Choruses
### Filed by Waluigi, Auditor-General of Acoustic Discipline and Harmonic Failures

*(Note: To browse all 18 songs in an interactive jukebox with WebAudio acoustic cues and category filter tabs, open **[Waluipedia's Grand Songbook](#/songs)**!)*

Waluigi has audited military budgets, planar fractures, and corporate trapdoors, but no phenomenon in 1040 BF has caused as much operational disruption as **unsanctioned singing**. Across 57 documented campaign records, Disaster Inc. and their allies have repeatedly broken into song during stealth infiltrations, while floating in barrels, and while standing outside locked doors. WAH!

---

## 1. Toad Shanties & Liberation Anthems

### We Are the Toads (The Vigilance Liberation Anthem)
- **Source**: [Kaelor Judi & The Road to Raventree](kaelor_judi_witness_line_and_the_road_to_raventree) / [Liberated Toads](liberated_toads)
- **Lyrics**: *"We are the Toads, we hold the line! / Through cannon smoke and engine whine! / From Mushroom Hall to Midland shore, / We will be captive Toads no more!"*
- **Campaign Context**: Sung by Toad refugees falling out of barrels and marching along the road after the airship *Vigilance* exploded and was seized by the Iron Legion.
- **Waluigi's Critique**: *"A military anthem sung by fungi in barrels. High spirit, zero harmonic discipline. WAH!"*

### The Toads Sing at the Door (Harvestide 14 Anthem)
- **Source**: [14 Harvestside — Rattles, Morel & The Watermelon](shadow_estate_session_Harvestside_14_full)
- **Lyrics**: *"Open up the iron door, / Markop's checking on the floor! / Eager's waiting with a blade, / In the Shadow Estate shade!"*
- **Campaign Context**: While Markop was delicately listening for magical traps behind an ancient door, the Toad escort cohort began singing a loud marching tune directly behind him.
- **Waluigi's Critique**: *"Toads do not understand doors. They believe every closed door is an invitation for an opera."*

### The Longjump Anthem (The Mario Retirement Shanty)
- **Source**: [The Mage's Embassy Ambush & Luigi Interrogation](the_embassy_ambush_and_luigi_interrogation)
- **Lyrics**: *"Oh, crouch on the stairs and watch your speed, / No more castles that you need! / Backwards jump through stone and wall, / And leave the kingdom once for all!"*
- **Campaign Context**: A popular underground tavern song that emerged after rumors spread of Mario backwards longjumping out of his heroic duties to retire on an eastern farm.
- **Waluigi's Critique**: *"The catchy folk song that drove Wario to kidnap Luigi. 10/10 chorus, 0/10 diplomatic aftermath."*

---

## 2. Unsanctioned Stealth-Ruining Choruses

### The Stealth-Ruining Chorus of the Grove of Woe
- **Source**: [The Grove of Woe Incident](the_grove_of_woe_incident)
- **Lyrics**: *"Oh, we're sneaking through the dark, / Not a footprint, not a mark! / Quiet as the shadows creep, / While the Mazebounds fall asleep... / (LOUDER!) OH WE'RE SNEAKING THROUGH THE DARK!"*
- **Campaign Context**: During an active stealth mission in the Grove of Woe, Green T asked if the Toads could start singing. Everyone joined in—including Remi while draped over Markop's shoulder—until Markop yelled for silence.
- **Waluigi's Critique**: *"The only stealth operation in recorded history where the infiltrators announced their own coordinates in four-part harmony."*

### The Singing Thief's Bedside Ballad
- **Source**: [The Dark Rooms & The Balcony Plan](feyward_dark_rooms_and_balcony_planning)
- **Lyrics**: *"Sleep now, wizard, close your eyes, / Underneath the purple skies. / Keep your spells and keep your pride, / I'll just take what's in your hide..."*
- **Campaign Context**: Sung softly by Purple T while Archie Miser was pinned to a bed, soothing the wizard while robbing his pockets blind.
- **Waluigi's Critique**: *"A lullaby with a 100% successful theft rate. Utterly shameless."*

---

## 3. Feywild Drinking Shanties & Unleaving Earworms

### We Rolled

Into Raventree on a Tuesday Maybe Thursday
- **Source**: [The Overgrown Manor Campaign](overgrown_manor_campaign)
- **Lyrics**: *"We rolled into Raventree on a Tuesday maybe Thursday! / The wine was already flowing and the grapes were getting hazy! / The lady said one night would last a thousand happy years, / So drink the poisoned honey and forget your mortal fears!"*
- **Campaign Context**: A satyr revelry shanty sung in the overgrown Feywild gardens of Raventree Manor, accompanied by alcoholic honey that knocks out adventurers.
- **Waluigi's Critique**: *"A drinking song designed to make you forget what century it is so they can steal your boots."*

### Saedia's Music Box Melody (The Unleaving Earworm)
- **Source**: [The Overgrown Manor Campaign](overgrown_manor_campaign)
- **Lyrics**: *(Instrumental — a delicate, haunting crystalline waltz in 3/4 time that repeats indefinitely inside the listener's mind)*
- **Campaign Context**: Saedia wound up a small music box in the manor gardens. The melody permanently lodged itself in Waluigi's brain and has refused to leave since.
- **Waluigi's Critique**: *"Waluigi has tried sleeping pills, loud tennis grunts, and Wario's snoring—nothing removes this waltz from my skull! WAH!"*

---

## 4. Waluigi's Acoustic Audit & Harmonic Verdict

Waluigi's acoustic verdict on Disaster Inc.'s musical discipline:
1. **Stealth Prohibition**: Four-part harmony is henceforth banned within 500 yards of any enemy checkpoint, Mazebound encampment, or Mages' Guild embassy.
2. **Toad Vocal Quarantine**: All Toad cohorts must be issued acoustic muzzles or garlic bread before approaching locked doors.
3. **The Wario Exception**: Wario's money chant (*"WAH-HA-HA! Give me the gold!"*) is legally classified as industrial noise rather than music.

---

## 5. Full-Length Broadway Showstoppers & Complete Camp Anthems

Waluigi has expanded this archive to include the **complete, unabridged lyrics, bridge solos, and stage directions** for the five most elaborate musical numbers in the campaign:
1. **The Iron Dominion Anthem: "Heroes Reborn" (A Staggering Circus)** — The Legion Stage Singer's 4-part Broadway roast of Archie, Hjumpik, Toad Lee, Toadburt, Dan, Bowser, Markop, and Remi.
2. **"We Creep Through the Halls (Toads With No Balls)" / "Reborn (Iron Remnant Remix)"** — The Liberated Toads' complete creeping chant and battle anthem.
3. **The Iron Dominion Refined: "Yesterday's Stain"** — The smooth, venomous show-host taunt mocking the fellowship's second-rate courage.
4. **"The Revel Never Ends!" (The Satyr's Bender Hymn)** — Ralos / Relis / Pal's overgrown Feywild drinking anthem that pulls Hjumpik into a dance.
5. **Wario's Attic Heist: "Gimme the Loot, Gimme the Gold!"** — Wario's Solarium Bramblefly battle song, ending with a ticking present box and a splintering floor.

*(Open **[Waluipedia's Grand Songbook](#/songs)** and click the **📜 Full-Length Campaign Songs (5)** tab to read the complete lyrics and play their acoustic synth cues!)*

summary:
Junimus Gorolini Bongo Jr. — known publicly and permanently as Chunky Kong — was mourned at a state funeral that functioned simultaneously as a grief ceremony, a political earthquake, a cabinet restructuring, and a preview of everything this war is about to cost.

Diddy Kong gave the eulogy first. He spoke about Chunky's 26 billion in personal charity. About libraries and schools and hospitals. About a man who struck gold and gave every last penny of it away because he loved people. Diddy cried. He was not embarrassed about it.

Wario arrived late, announced himself, apologized for nothing, and then gave a eulogy that was honest in a way that people who hate Wario do not expect from him. He described Chunky covering his throat surgery costs without a second question. He described Chunky saying roughly translated that throat surgery sounds like the absolute worst and nobody should go into that alone. Wario said he wished for Decayd to recover. He sounded, by the end, like he was trying very hard not to cry. He did not fully succeed.

Cranky Kong arrived in chains, said something about blood and steel girders and a nosebleed that had no business being at a funeral, and was removed still in chains still asking for water.

Lanky Kong arrived. He had been warned. He promised no fooling. He told the aristocrats joke at a children's funeral. He was excommunicated from the Kongo Bongo state apparatus effective immediately. He was stripped of his vestments. He was walked out.

And in the middle of everything Lanky was shouting, in the middle of everyone assuming he was drunk and disrespectful and beyond help — Lanky was trying to tell them something about Funky. That Funky was going to betray them. Nobody listened. Nobody was listening to Lanky by then. That was, perhaps, the point.

Funky Kong had stepped down that morning. He told Diddy this and Diddy told the room. Diddy did not want the joint position. He said give it to Funky. Funky had already gone.

Admiral Link of the Great Sea sent a HYAH of condolences and a gift basket of homemade soup in bottles, which arrived on time and was the most logistically competent condolence of the day.

In a broom closet somewhere in the building, if the intelligence is accurate, Chunky Kong was alive. Had been alive the whole time. Bones operating a fake death for purposes that Diddy was not informed about and that Waluigi is still in the process of understanding.

A funeral before a war. A preview of things to come. So many young Kongs and Kremlings about to be lost for cold-blooded ambition. Waluigi is documenting this because someone has to document it properly and because the record cannot lie about what happened here even when everyone involved would prefer a cleaner version. WAH.
description:
Waluigi did not attend this funeral in person. Waluigi is documenting it anyway because the record requires documentation regardless of whether Waluigi was present, and because multiple fragments of verified and partially verified testimony have reached Waluigi through channels that Waluigi considers sufficiently reliable to justify a full entry.

What follows is an account of one of the most significant events in Kongo Bongo's recent political history, dressed in the clothing of a funeral and containing within it the seeds of multiple crises that are still actively developing.

## What the Funeral Was Supposed to Be


Junimus Gorolini Bongo Jr. — known to everyone who loved him as Chunky — was by all accounts a genuinely extraordinary person.

Diddy Kong's eulogy provided the public record of this and Waluigi treats it as accurate because Diddy does not perform emotion he does not feel. The numbers alone are staggering: approximately 26 billion out of his own pocket directed toward roads, hospitals, schools, libraries. More than the combined income of all Congo Bongo citizens including the prime minister. A man who struck gold — genuinely, actually struck gold in the world through means not fully documented but apparently legitimate — and then gave every last penny of it back to the people around him because he loved them.

Waluigi has documented many wealthy individuals over the course of this crisis. Wario is rich through accumulation and retention. Waluigi is not going to pretend Wario gives his money away with Chunky's generosity. Chunky Kong appears to have been a genuinely different category of wealthy person: one who treated personal wealth as a public resource. This is rare. This is worth documenting explicitly rather than implying.

Diddy's full eulogy described this. He cried. He was not embarrassed. He said Chunky was probably eating all those bananas in heaven like he said he would and he hoped they never ran out up there. Waluigi finds this sentiment straightforward and sincere and documents it as such without analysis because some things do not require analysis.

The funeral was supposed to be about that man. About that life. About what those 26 billion built and what the people who received it felt about losing the person who gave it.

Instead it was also about Cranky Kong in chains. Lanky Kong and the aristocrats joke. Wario arriving late and being surprisingly human about it. A cabinet restructuring that nobody had scheduled. A war that everyone could feel approaching. And a question, planted by the chaos of Lanky's removal, about whether the loudest most disrespectful person in the room was trying to warn them about something real.

## Wario:


The Part Nobody Expected

Wario arrived late. This is consistent with Wario's documented approach to every event he attends. Wario does not arrive on time because Wario operates on Wario time, which is calibrated to maximize his own convenience without regard for the inconvenience this causes others.

He announced himself. He confirmed he was not late by his own assessment. He asked the room to give him one second.

Diddy warned him. No funny stuff. You're not in Wario Land right now.

Wario said he was actually pretty sad about this one.

Diddy pointed out that Wario had tried robbing Chunky of millions.

Wario said, and Waluigi is quoting this directly because it is one of the more accurate self-assessments Wario has ever produced: associating with me guarantees robbing at least once. Everybody on this planet knows that.

This is true. This is documentably, verifiably, historically true. Waluigi can provide citations going back decades.

Diddy pushed further. He said Chunky was brilliant but made terrible misjudgments that sometimes made him look stupid. He said Wario was a troublemaker who preyed on a kind man's heart when his brain had its back turned.

Wario's response: 'Holy — that's good rhetoric. I will quote you on it without stating the source someday probably.'

This is also consistent with Wario. Wario recognizes quality when he encounters it regardless of whether the quality is aimed at him.

Wario was then told he was being recorded. His response to this — 'I could have said some extremely incriminating things' and the request to be edited out of the final product to save on runtime — is Wario performing self-awareness about his own incrimination risk while simultaneously knowing the self-awareness itself is being recorded. Wario contains layers. Waluigi does not always enjoy this.

Then Wario spoke about Kremling doctrine. His knowledge of Kremling legal loopholes and self-imposed taboos had apparently been instrumental in previous cases. Diddy acknowledged this. Wario explained his motivation: these guys are bastards. He had been happy to frustrate them with their own legal framework as often as his memory could provide.

This is Wario as he actually functions. Not the cartoon villain who wants treasure and nothing else. A man who has genuine hatreds, genuine loyalties, genuine knowledge that he deploys with genuine enthusiasm when the target merits it. The Kremlings apparently merit it. Wario's institutional knowledge of Kremling Code — specifically that an amendment to Kremling Code incurs immediate death penalty upon ratification — had been used as a weapon against them repeatedly.

Waluigi finds this professionally interesting and files it alongside the broader Kremling legal doctrine analysis from the Second Summit entry.

Then Wario's actual eulogy.

He began formally. 'Hello. This is Wario. Chunky and I both shared a passion for international law.'

He mentioned his throat surgery. He had needed it. He had delayed it because of council commitments. He had been doing a motivational speech for the Kong legal partners when he told Chunky the news backstage. And Junky — Chunky — without skipping a beat had offered to cover the costs and recommended an excellent surgeon.

Chunky had said, roughly translated: throat surgery sounds like the absolute worst. Nobody should have to go through that alone. That's what friends are there for.

Wario said it was the worst and most unnecessary surgery for a specific type of cancer that Waluigi will not reproduce here for reasons of taste. But with Chunky looking out for him he was able to pull through.

Wario said he wished for Decay — which Waluigi interprets as a figure connected to Chunky's situation — to recover. He said thank you. He said goodbye.

He was choked up by the end. Not fully crying. Trying not to cry. The eulogy was honest in a way that the people who categorize Wario as objectively evil were not prepared for.

Waluigi has documented Wario across many events and many crises. Wario's grief is real when he experiences it. He does not perform grief he does not feel because performing unnecessary vulnerability is not in Wario's operational model. If Wario appeared to be trying not to cry, Wario was actually trying not to cry. If Wario said Chunky was a close friend, Chunky was a close friend.

This does not make Wario a good person. Wario is not a good person by most frameworks Waluigi would apply to that designation. Wario will rob you, exploit you, use your kindness against you, and then eat your snacks without apology. But Wario is also capable of genuine attachment, genuine loss, and genuine attempts to honor the dead in the moments when it costs him something to do so.

The funeral of Chunky Kong is a situation where Wario's genuine attachment was visible and his attempt to honor it was more successful than most of the room managed. This is documented.

## Cranky Kong:


The Chains, the Story, and the Request for Water

Cranky Kong arrived.

Diddy's reaction on being told was: 'Are you?' which is the sound of a man who had hoped this particular problem would not materialize and has now received confirmation that it has.

Cranky had been extradited. Or had extradited himself. Or had simply arrived despite the outstanding charges, which include being the senile would-be assassin of the prime minister awaiting trial with multiple prior convictions. These charges are apparently real and apparently active.

Cranky began his remarks by addressing the audience as having a lot of stupid faces. He referenced people back in his day. He mentioned Wario. He mentioned 'Mario pansy Jumpman at the time' which required being shut up about because apparently historical context around that name is complicated. He began telling a story involving steel girders, barrels, darkness, a woman screaming, and a physical incident involving his own person that resulted in a nosebleed and the specific absence of something that usually accompanies such injuries.

He was cut off. Correctly.

He was told to get back to his cage. He protested. He asked for water. He was taken out still in chains.

Waluigi notes one significant element that gets lost in the general chaos of Cranky's appearance: his mention of DK hiding his original Coconut Gun. This is internal Kong family intelligence that suggests specific conflict over specific objects within the family structure. The Coconut Gun is significant enough to hide from Cranky deliberately. Why Cranky would want it, and why DK chose to conceal it rather than simply deny Cranky access through other means, is a question Waluigi files for future investigation.

## Lanky Kong:


The Aristocrats, the Excommunication, and the Warning Nobody Heard

This section requires Waluigi to do something uncomfortable, which is present two contradictory interpretations of the same behavior simultaneously and refuse to fully resolve the contradiction because the evidence does not permit resolution.

Lanky Kong had been warned. Explicitly. He came in requesting assurance that this was not a joke. He asked everyone to promise. He made them say it. Promise. He received the promise.

Then he told the aristocrats joke. At a children's funeral. About a man whose family was in the room mourning him.

The surface reading: Lanky was drunk, or immature, or incapable of grasping that someone he was genuinely connected to was actually dead, or some combination of all three. His behavior was disrespectful in a way that caused real harm to people in real grief. Diddy's response — the fury, the excommunication, the stripping of vestments, the forcible removal — was a proportionate response to what Lanky had done in that room.

Lanky had history with Chunky. DK had referenced this in the leaked phone call. History means genuine connection. Genuine connection does not excuse the joke. But it does create a question about WHY Lanky chose that specific moment for that specific behavior.

Now: the other reading.

Lanky was shouting something when he was being removed. He was shouting it with the urgency of someone trying to communicate something before the window closed. And what Lanky was apparently shouting — before he was drowned out and walked out — was something about Funky.

Funky Kong had stepped down that morning.

This is the detail that recontextualizes everything. Funky stepped down on the morning of Chunky's funeral. He told Diddy. Diddy announced it. The room processed it with the shock of an unexpected political development landing on top of an already overwhelming grief event.

Funky stepping down is not a small thing. Funky is not a minor figure. Funky is — was — a central pillar of the Kongo Bongo political structure. His departure on this specific morning, at this specific moment, before a war, is either a coincidence or it is not.

Lanky appeared to believe it was not.

Lanky was shouting about Funky while being excommunicated. The room heard 'Lanky is causing a scene.' Lanky may have been saying 'Funky is going to betray you.' These are not the same thing and the second one, if accurate, is significantly more important than the first.

Waluigi cannot confirm what Lanky knew or how he knew it or whether what he believed was accurate. What Waluigi can document is this: Lanky arrived at the funeral specifically asking whether it was a joke, specifically needing reassurance, specifically requesting a promise. This is not the behavior of someone indifferent to the proceedings. Something was disturbing Lanky before he arrived. His subsequent behavior may have been an attempt to communicate a warning using the only platform he had in that moment, which was the platform of causing a scene large enough to generate attention before he was removed.

If Lanky was drunk, the warning still deserved to be heard.
If Lanky was unstable, the warning still deserved to be assessed.
If Lanky was right about Funky, the room's decision to excommunicate him and remove him before he finished speaking may have cost them the intelligence they most needed.

Waluigi does not know. Waluigi documents the question and flags it for ongoing monitoring.

The excommunication itself was procedurally legitimate. Diddy inherited the joint position of attorney general and secretary of state through Chunky's death. Funky's departure meant the position defaulted to Diddy rather than the person Diddy would have preferred to receive it. One of the first acts of that joint position was removing Lanky from every office he held in the Kongo Bongo state.

Dirty. Lying. Perverted. Sick. Drunk bastard. These were the words used. Bismerching the memory of a beloved member of the DK crew. Balloonifying himself and getting high off his own head rushes. No right to call himself the tropical medical patriarch of the Kong Island church.

Stripped. Effective immediately. Get out.

Funky walked him from the premises. Told him to stay out of trouble. Said if I ever see you again it better be on the upswing.

Lanky left.

And whatever Lanky was trying to say about Funky left with him.

## Funky Kong:


The Resignation Nobody Fully Explained

Funky stepped down.

This is the hardest fact in this entry to analyze because the testimony about the resignation is thinner than everything else. What is documented: Funky told Diddy he was stepping down. On the morning of the funeral. Diddy did not want the resulting position. He said give it to Funky. Funky was already gone.

Funky had also, in the moments before the funeral proceedings formally began, indicated to someone — the transcript is unclear on exactly who was hearing this — that the war was coming. That the people gathered needed some days to heal first. That if the crisis hit Kongo Bongo Country without those healing days, the country was about to get a beating.

That is the voice of someone who knows something about what is coming. Not fear. Preparation. Funky was speaking like a man who had already made his decisions and was trying to give the people around him enough time and information to make theirs.

Why Funky stepped down remains unresolved.

Possibilities Waluigi is holding simultaneously without resolving:

Funky stepped down because the position was not survivable given what he knew was coming and he was protecting Diddy by ensuring Diddy had the power to act rather than inheriting a burned shell.

Funky stepped down because he was preparing to act in a capacity that his official position would have prevented or complicated.

Funky stepped down because he knew something about the broader political situation — possibly something connected to what Lanky was trying to warn about — that made remaining in office untenable for reasons he was not prepared to explain publicly.

Funky stepped down because the weight of it, all of it, was too much for one day and he needed to not be in a position of power for reasons that have nothing to do with strategy.

Waluigi does not know which is true. The timing is too specific to be casual. The morning of the funeral. Before the proceedings. After telling Diddy but before Diddy could respond with anything but shock.

Funky also had a condition Waluigi is documenting with care and without the label that was suggested by observers because the label is not Waluigi's to apply. What Waluigi can document is that Funky had involuntary vocalizations during the proceedings. These happened. They were part of who Funky was in that room on that day. The people who love Funky know this about him and it does not change what he said or what he meant.

The room heard his voice saying he wished the big guy could be there. Meaning Chunky. Meaning the man in the casket.

Funky said he agreed. He said he missed Chunky. He said it as someone who had made peace with the loss and had not made peace with it simultaneously, which is the only way grief works in real time.

Waluigi records this with respect and without irony.

## The Broom Closet: What Diddy Did Not Know


Waluigi is going to document this section with the explicit caveat that the intelligence supporting it is of uncertain provenance and that what follows is either the most important fact in this entire entry or a fabrication sophisticated enough to waste significant amounts of Waluigi's analytical attention.

At the end of the funeral. After the speeches. After Lanky was removed and Cranky was extracted and Wario had said what he came to say and the room was beginning to breathe again.

There was a conversation in or near a broom closet.

The voice in the conversation said to Chunky: how's it going, man.

And there was a response. And laughter.

The voice told Chunky that he had not been broadcasting to anyone. That the confessional was a distraction. That nobody was watching. That it was just a broom closet. That Chunky had been kept there specifically. That the death was faked.

The voice said Chunky's family was taken care of. That Diddy had taken his place on the cabinet, meaning Diddy did not know. That the charity programs were running smoothly. That attention to them was at an all-time high because of Diddy's work.

The voice said it had plans. Big plans. That it was sorry for pulling the crocodile skin over Chunky's eyes for a little while. But trust me on this one.

Chunky Kong is not dead.

Chunky Kong is alive in a broom closet while the world mourns him, while his family grieves in closed casket because they told everyone he was shot in public and spilled out in front of everybody, while Diddy gives eulogies and cries real tears and means every word.

Diddy did not know. The voice said this explicitly. Way I played it. Nobody knows.

Waluigi does not know who the voice belongs to. The testimony is insufficient for identification. The voice references a woman who had all the range — that backstabbing — with a laugh that does not resolve into a name. The voice says it does not do screaming, which is a personality marker that Waluigi is filing.

What Waluigi knows: if this is real, Chunky's death was staged by someone with enough access and operational capacity to fake a public assassination, maintain a controlled environment for a living person for an extended period, ensure that family charity programs continued operating, and position Diddy into the cabinet role without revealing the deception to Diddy himself.

That is not a small operation. That is an intelligence operation of considerable sophistication executed during a public funeral for the person who is the subject of the operation.

And it was executed in a building where Wario gave an honest eulogy, Cranky Kong demanded water in chains, Lanky Kong was excommunicated for trying to warn someone about something, and Funky Kong had already quietly stepped down and left.

Waluigi suspects all of these events are connected. Waluigi cannot yet prove it.

## Admiral Link's Soup


Admiral Link of the Great Sea of Hyrule sent a HYAH of condolences and a gift basket containing bottles of homemade soup.

The soup arrived on time. The gift basket was logistically well-executed. The HYAH was sincere by all accounts.

Waluigi documents this because it was the most competent condolence of the day and because decency, when it appears in documentation, deserves to be noted alongside everything else.

## The War That Is Coming


A funeral before a war.

This is what Funky said in the opening moments. This is what the funeral was. Chunky Kong was genuinely extraordinary by all documented accounts, and he is being mourned by people who loved him, and the mourning is real, and the loss is real.

And in the middle of all of it Waluigi can see the shape of what comes next.

Young Kongs who have never fought a real war. Young Kremlings who have been directed toward this conflict by cold-blooded ambition operating through institutional channels and information warfare. People who will die not because they chose this but because the people above them on various political structures made decisions that produced this outcome as a consequence.

The Second Summit produced ships full of relief supplies and diplomatic wreckage simultaneously. The funeral of Chunky Kong produced genuine grief, a cabinet restructuring, an excommunication, a warning that may have been a betrayal warning, a fake death operation, and homemade soup from the Great Sea.

All of it is moving in the same direction.

Waluigi does not know how many people are going to die in the coming conflict between Kongo Bongo and the Kremlings. Waluigi does not know whether Lanky's warning about Funky was accurate. Waluigi does not know whether the person in the broom closet with Chunky is operating a legitimate intelligence program or something darker. Waluigi does not know whether Funky's resignation was protective or preparatory or something else entirely.

Waluigi knows that Chunky Kong was mourned today by people who loved him genuinely, including a man in overalls who tried not to cry and mostly failed.

Waluigi knows that the war is coming regardless of how good the soup was.

Waluigi documents everything.

WAH.

description:
Waluigi has assembled this account from field reports, intercepted communication fragments, Bowser's own retelling — which required approximately sixty percent deflation to reach plausible truth — and the testimony of several Toads who witnessed portions of the events and remain, by all accounts, traumatized. The events described here represent one of the most comprehensive tactical disintegrations Waluigi has ever documented. Not because the enemy was overwhelming. Not because the mission parameters changed beyond recognition. But because the party's own decision-making degenerated into a cascade of impulse, stubbornness, misplaced confidence, and the particular chemistry of people who care about each other but cannot agree on what caring MEANS.

Waluigi would like to state for the record: this is what happens when you put a teenager with a gun and a history of shooting people she shouldn't, a centaur healer with a savior complex and the patience of a saint being slowly ground into dust, a king with abandonment issues and more combat capability than emotional regulation, a former crime lord who thinks assassination is mentorship, and a collection of Toads who believe singing solves problems into a hostile supernatural environment and tell them to 'figure it out.'

They figured it out. They figured out how to make everything worse in ways that will take MONTHS to untangle — assuming anyone survives to do the untangling.

## Context:


The Birthday Trap Aftermath and the Tanuki Problem

The events documented here are a DIRECT CONTINUATION of the Birthday Trap incident. Readers unfamiliar with that incident should consult the relevant article, but Waluigi will provide the essential context because this context is the FUEL for everything that followed.

Vostolas the Archivist organized a surprise birthday party for Remi involving caged Toads, a tanuki disguised as Toadburt, a cursed cake designed to place her permanently under Onyx Hand control, and a trapdoor. The party identified the trap before Remi entered, extracted the fake Toadburt, exposed him as a tanuki, debated whether to kill him, accidentally shot Eager in the process, considered slavery as a compromise position, watched democracy collapse entirely, freed the tanuki into a bathroom over Remi's furious objections, and then Remi was angry that she did not get to cast what she believed should have been the deciding vote on whether to execute the prisoner.

The key dynamics from that incident:

Green T wanted execution. Operational security. Loose ends. The logic of a crime lord who has survived by not leaving witnesses. He handed Remi a silenced revolver, told her she needed to be stronger, and framed execution as education.

Remi was willing to execute. She pressed a loaded revolver against the tanuki's head and pulled the trigger before Markop intervened — pulling the gun upward at the same moment Eager bumped into Markop, causing the bullet to graze Eager instead.

Markop wanted mercy. He delivered the devastating moral argument: 'Remi, three people have betrayed you. You didn't shoot them.' He identified that Remi was not shooting traitors — she was shooting people she COULD shoot.

Bowser drew a line. He objected when Green T armed Remi. He punched Remi to stop her from firing. He said: 'That's brutal, even for me.' Then he voted to kill but ALLOWED mercy because Hjumpik would have wanted mercy. The gap between wanting and allowing is where character lives.

The tanuki was freed into a bathroom. Markop untied him and let him go.

Remi was furious. Not about the outcome — about the process. She wanted to VOTE. She wanted her vote to COUNT. The vote she wanted to cast was to kill the prisoner.

This is the emotional context. A party that had just argued about killing a tied-up shapeshifter, accidentally shot one of their own members, and released a prisoner over the objections of their youngest member who wanted blood. Trust was fractured. Remi was angry about process. Green T had just armed a child and framed execution as education. Markop had just delivered a moral argument nobody wanted to hear. Bowser had just demonstrated that he carries Hjumpik with him in moments of decision.

The tanuki was in the bathroom.

And then things got worse.

## The Locked Room and the Lesson


Markop secured the tanuki. He shut the bathroom door, locked it from his side, and made certain the shapeshifter was contained. This was deliberate and careful — the action of someone who has finally learned that leaving loose ends in a haunted manor produces complications requiring stitches.

With the tanuki locked away — the same tanuki who had just been the subject of an execution debate, the same tanuki whose life had been spared over Remi's explicit objection, the same tanuki who was still breathing only because Markop pulled a gun upward and Bowser invoked the memory of Hjumpik — Green T turned his attention to Remi.

Waluigi needs to discuss Green T's approach to mentorship because it explains everything that followed.

Green T is a former crime lord who ran the Tea Leaf Syndicate through tea service and curtains. He survived the fireball that destroyed his organization, watched Earl Grey explode, lost everything he had built, and responded to each humiliation by becoming SHARPER. He is not evil in the cartoonish sense. He is practical in ways that look like evil from certain angles. He shot the Shadow Anchor from the children's table. He destroyed Remi's invisible ring by seeing something nobody else could see. His instinct is always to find the angle that avoids the obvious confrontation — or, when confrontation is unavoidable, to ensure the person doing the confronting is properly trained.

Green T told Remi she needed to focus better. That even if someone pulled her away — as Markop had pulled the gun away during the tanuki incident — she could not miss her shots. He asked the rhetorical question that hung in the air like smoke: what if that had been a bad guy instead of a tied-up shapeshifter?

The question answered itself. If it had been a bad guy, Remi would have missed, the bad guy would not have missed, and the Toads would be writing condolence letters.

Green T handed her a sheet of paper. A Bros Attack — a cooperative combat technique where one party member assists another to amplify effectiveness. The specific technique was a support-fire maneuver: Green T would steady Remi's aim, adjust her positioning, and coordinate timing so her shots landed with greater force and accuracy. The concept is sound. The execution requires practice, timing, and the kind of mutual trust that is difficult to build when one member of the pair has already shot someone she wasn't supposed to shoot.

The instruction sheet was, by all accounts, a simple childish drawing. Stick figures. Arrows indicating direction of fire. A smiling face next to 'GOOD' and a frowning face next to 'BAD.' Green T had calibrated his instructional materials to Remi's comprehension level, which Waluigi considers both pragmatic and slightly devastating.

Remi studied the paper. She understood it. Then she looked at the locked bathroom door — the door behind which the tanuki was sitting, alive, because the party had voted mercy over her objection — and said she thought they should test the technique on 'this guy.'

Waluigi needs to sit with the implications of this. Remi was angry that she did not get to vote on the tanuki's execution. The vote happened without her. Mercy won. The tanuki was freed into the bathroom. And now, given a new weapon — not a gun this time but a TECHNIQUE, a method for making her shots count — Remi's first instinct was to use it on the person who had been spared.

This is not random violence. This is FRUSTRATED AGENCY seeking an outlet. Remi was denied her democratic participation in the decision to kill the tanuki. She was angry about the process, not the outcome. And now she had a process of her own — the Bros Attack — and she wanted to apply it to the unfinished business behind that bathroom door.

Markop, who had been organizing supplies, asked what she meant. Remi held up the Bros Attack sheet and explained she had gotten a paper on how to shoot better. Waluigi notes the enthusiasm — the specific energy of a child showing off a gold star, completely disconnected from the fact that the 'gold star' was a cooperative combat technique and the proposed test subject was a prisoner of war whose life she had just been denied permission to end. Markop asked to see the paper. She handed it to him. The Toads crowded around, staring at the stick-figure diagram with the intensity of military analysts examining battle plans.

For a moment, there was the illusion of order — a team reviewing tactical documentation and preparing a measured response. Then Markop looked at the locked bathroom door. Then he looked at Remi. Then he looked at the door again.

Eager told the Toads to guard the front entrance door — the main door to their current position, not the bathroom. Waluigi notes the distinction because it matters: Eager was thinking about EXTERNAL threats. The undead. The Voss servants. The things in the hallway. He was establishing perimeter security at the correct chokepoint. The Toads responded with 'not on our watch,' which is a phrase Waluigi has heard approximately four hundred times and which has never once prevented the thing they were watching from happening.

Remi aimed at the bathroom door.

## The Second Shooting:


The Tanuki Takes Another Hit

Markop objected immediately. They should not be attacking where a tied-up person was, he said, and he was correct. This was the reasonable, ethical, tactically sound position. Firing a weapon at a barricaded door behind which a restrained individual was sitting — the SAME individual whose life had been spared less than a day ago through divine mercy invoked in the name of an absent friend — was, by any standard of conduct, a terrible idea.

Salam, meanwhile, barricaded the entrance to their current position while everyone else argued. This is the kind of quietly competent action that goes unnoticed when louder people are debating whether to shoot prisoners through doors. Salam's instinct to fortify rather than attack was correct. Nobody acknowledged it. Nobody ever acknowledges it. Salam performs essential tactical functions in silence and receives trust questions about whether his money is a trick. Waluigi sees Salam. Waluigi documents Salam. Someone has to.

Remi aimed. Green T, honoring the spirit of the Bros Attack technique, nudged her aim down slightly. The adjustment was small — a matter of degrees. The difference between center mass on a door and lower center mass on a door behind which the tanuki — a shapeshifter who had impersonated their friend, yes, but who was also TIED UP and UNARMED and whose life had been DEMOCRATICALLY SPARED — was sitting.

A shot was fired. The door broke. A scream was heard.

The tanuki. Again. The same tanuki who had survived the execution debate, who had been freed into the bathroom by Markop, who had been locked in by Markop, who was probably sitting in there wondering whether the bathroom was any safer than the birthday trap he had been extracted from. Shot through a door.

Green T's Bros Attack worked. The shot was more accurate than Remi's unaided fire. The coordination improved her effectiveness. The technique functioned exactly as designed — against a prisoner who could not move, who had already been spared once, whose continued existence was supposed to represent the party's capacity for mercy.

Markop rushed to the scene. He healed the tanuki. He untied him. He ordered the party to leave the area immediately. The tanuki survived — barely — and was evacuated from the room in a state that Waluigi can only describe as 'justifiably furious at everyone involved and probably reconsidering every life choice that led to impersonating a Toad in a haunted manor.'

Waluigi wonders what the tanuki is thinking right now, wherever it is. It was hired to impersonate Toadburt. It was exposed. It was wrapped in a rug. A child pressed a gun to its head and pulled the trigger. The bullet grazed someone else instead. It was debated over like livestock. It was freed into a bathroom. It was locked in the bathroom. And then it was shot through the door by the same child using a new technique.

The tanuki's experience of Disaster Inc. is a concentrated version of what every person adjacent to this group eventually endures: you think the crisis is over, and then it gets worse in a direction you could not have predicted.

## The Confiscation and the Argument


Hours passed. The incident settled into the kind of tense silence that follows when everyone in a group knows something deeply wrong just happened and nobody wants to be the first to address it directly.

Then Markop reached for the gun.

The action was deliberate. Markop — four hooves, equine body, horse head with dark intelligent eyes that miss NOTHING — extended his hand toward the weapon Remi was carrying. His intent was clear: confiscation. Remi resisted. There was a struggle. Hands grabbed at the weapon. The party's healer and its most dangerous liability locked in physical contest over a gun.

Markop won. He is a centaur. Four-legged stability is both literal and metaphorical. Remi is a teenager. Physics and moral authority both favored Markop.

Dan offered the only appropriate commentary: 'Dang... that was pretty brutal.'

Markop told Remi she could not use that gun anymore. This was her second time. His voice was firm — the voice of someone drawing a line that should have been drawn earlier but that nobody had the authority or the willingness to draw until a shapeshifter was shot through a bathroom door.

Remi's defense was immediate: the tanuki had pretended to be their friend.

Markop's response was devastating in its precision. Three people had betrayed Remi, he said. She did not shoot them.

Waluigi has documented this argument in the Birthday Trap article, but its repetition here matters because of what Remi said NEXT. She said the three actual traitors were not betraying her — they were 'just having a rough time.' And then she said those people had MADE the tanuki pretend to be their friend, constructing a chain of culpability that absolved the masterminds and condemned the puppet.

The logic is circular and self-serving and deeply human. Remi cannot bring herself to hold the powerful accountable — the people who actually orchestrated the betrayals, who designed the traps, who erected the systems of control — because confronting power requires confronting the possibility that power cannot be reasoned with. It is easier to shoot the puppet than to face the puppeteer. The tanuki is small, contained, and helpless. The Onyx Hand is vast, diffuse, and everywhere. Remi's violence flows downhill, toward the weakest available target, because uphill violence is terrifying and uncertain.

Waluigi recognizes this pattern because Waluigi has seen it in kingdoms. He has seen it in empires. He has seen it in the Regal Empire's entire approach to governance: punish the visible, manageable, containable offender while the architects of suffering remain untouched in their administrative towers. Remi is not doing this consciously. She is doing it because it is the default setting of every frightened person who has been given a weapon and told to use it.

Salam, at the perimeter, heard footsteps approaching the barricaded doors. He reported arrows — his and Eager's. He sensed the approaching figures were undead.

Green T showed Remi how to properly hold the gun — if she was going to carry it again, which Markop had not yet authorized but which the tactical situation might require. He showed her how to aim. He put it away.

Remi thought about shooting the undead at the door. She didn't.

Waluigi considers this the single most significant moment of personal growth Remi has demonstrated in the entire Raventree operation. She had a weapon. She had targets. She had justification. And she chose not to fire. Whether this was because of Green T's training, Markop's confiscation, or simply exhaustion, the result was the same: Remi made a decision that did not involve a bullet.

Waluigi does not know if this represents lasting change or a temporary pause in an escalating pattern. But he documents it because it happened.

## The Wedding


Invitation: A Masterwork of Aristocratic Menace

The party moved through what witnesses describe as the 'Moneybags Jungle' — a dense, overgrown area that Salam found conflicting for reasons unspecified in Waluigi's sources. They descended to a lower level. A guard — rushed, breathless, operating under time pressure — intercepted them.

The guard was delighted to see Remi. Just in time for the wedding, the guard said, and handed her a paper.

Waluigi has obtained a copy of this document. He has read it seven times. Each reading has produced a different emotion, ranging from professional admiration for the calligraphy to volcanic fury at its contents.

The invitation was issued BY DECREE OF THE HOUSE OF VOSS from SUNLESS KEEP, RAVENTREE VALE. It announced A Sacred and Eternal Union between Remi — identified as Ward of the Shadowmere Compact — and Lord Malachar Voss, Third Inheritor of the Onyx Throne, Warden of the Sunless Keep.

Waluigi will analyze the key elements because beneath the ornate script and theatrical language lies a legally sophisticated instrument of coercion that would make the Regal Empire's contract lawyers weep with professional envy.

**The wardship claim.** Remi is identified as a 'Ward of the Shadowmere Compact.' The word 'ward' is critical. A ward is not a free person. A ward is someone whose legal autonomy has been delegated to a custodial authority. If the Shadowmere Compact holds wardship over Remi, then Remi's consent to the marriage is, under whatever legal framework the Compact operates within, IRRELEVANT. The custodian consents on behalf of the ward. The ward attends. This is not a proposal. This is a notification of proceedings already concluded.

**The waiting.** The phrase 'has waited the appropriate span of mortal decades for the ward to reach her appointed ascendance' is one of the most disturbing sentences Waluigi has read in a career that includes Shroob invasion manuals, Afton research protocols, and Iron Legion processing doctrine. Lord Voss — an entity old enough to measure time in 'mortal decades' — has been WAITING for Remi to reach a specific age or state. This marriage was arranged before Remi was old enough to understand the concept of marriage. Possibly before she was born. The phrase 'His appetite for this occasion knows no restraint' is a line Waluigi will not analyze further because his therapist has specifically asked him to avoid dwelling on phrasing that activates what she calls his 'protective rage spiral.'

**The weaponized guest list.** Archie Miser is invited as 'Guest of Honor.' Lord Bowser is listed as 'Recognized Dignitary of the Shell Throne.' Green T receives the chilling note: 'Whom We Are Most Delighted to Welcome Back.' Waluigi himself is listed as 'Chronicler of the Recent Unpleasantness.'

The problem is not that any single decision was wrong. The problem is that correct decisions made by people with incompatible priorities produce INCORRECT outcomes.

Markop prioritized protection. Bowser prioritized loyalty. Remi prioritized the mission. Green T prioritized training. Salam prioritized trust verification.

Every one of them was right. And the aggregate result of all of them being right was a party scattered across two planes of existence with no healer, no plan, and a vampire wedding approaching.

This is the fundamental paradox of group operations: individual correctness does not guarantee collective success. You can have five people making five good decisions and produce a result worse than if one idiot had made all the decisions alone, because at least the idiot would have been CONSISTENT.

Disaster Inc. is held together less by belief than by repeated survival. Every time the universe should have broken them and did not, the bond thickened. Not because they became healthier. Because they became harder to separate. This incident separated them anyway.

The tanuki was shot twice. Spared twice. Shot through a door by the person who was denied the vote to kill it. Healed twice by the person who denied the vote. And somewhere in a bathroom in Raventree Manor, a shapeshifter who impersonated a Toad for a birthday trap is probably wondering whether any amount of money was worth getting involved with these people.

Remi needs the scythe. Bowser needs Markop. Markop needs his axe. Salam needs to trust someone. Green T needs to not be 'welcomed back' by vampires. The Toads need to stop singing. The tanuki needs a therapist.

None of these needs are compatible with each other. None can be sacrificed without consequence. And the clock — both literal and matrimonial — is ticking.

The wedding invitation said: 'Survival is a courtesy, not a guarantee.'

Waluigi considers this the most honest thing the House of Voss has ever written.

And somewhere in a collapsing library in another dimension, the King of the Koopas is standing over the body of a man he just beat nearly to death, holding a photograph that connects to a conspiracy he doesn't understand, carrying a badge bearing his own insignia that he did not authorize, in a room full of books he can't read, with a portal that won't reopen behind him.

Bowser's response to this situation will probably involve punching something.

Waluigi is, against his better judgment, rooting for him.

Because what else is there?

WAH.
